correctness.rationale: The Boolean images of atoms partition the domain, yielding the unique inverse-image map. Testing singletons in D1 forces the image of every source class to be one entire target class. Below k the threshold test is vacuous. For a source of size at least k and a smaller target of size below k, the whole target disproves preservation. If the target has at least k elements and there is a duplicated preimage, k−1 target points including that value lift to at least k source points, again a contradiction. This proves the exact dichotomy and shows that only classes of size k release new maps when k increases by one. The product and inclusion–exclusion formulas are over labeled classes; the Boolean image has size 2^{|f(X)|}. Idempotence fixes every selected class pointwise, so the remaining classes choose independently, with one compulsory choice for each large size and for the global minimum when small classes exist. This gives the displayed support count and the worked example. The run-together case break at RESULT.md line 26 is typographical; lines 12–15 and 72 unambiguously specify the two distinct weights.
residual_risks: Independent enumeration uses 11 class-size multisets through four points and one six-point profile (1,2,3), with labeled class supports within each representative. It does not re-run the package's larger recorded enumeration; it supplements the all-size proof.

value.rationale: One counting grade between the ordinary existential modality and full graded rigidity gives an exact, size-dependent change in the allowed self-maps. The precise strictness criterion and the resulting compulsory-size supports answer which finite equivalence classes can survive retraction under a minimal graded expansion. They distinguish genuinely active thresholds on mixed-size frames and are not the D1 support census relabeled.
residual_risks: The result is a finite labeled-frame classification only; no general statement on the pure single-D_k language or arbitrary frames is inferred.
